chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Safwan ibn Yahya, who said:

I asked Abu Al-Hassan (peace be upon him) about passing by at the rear of the Masjid of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) and not offering greetings to the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family). So he (peace be upon him) said: 'Abu Al-Hassan (peace be upon him) did not do that.' I said: 'So he (peace be upon him) would enter the Masjid and offer greetings from afar, not approaching the grave?' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'No.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Offer greetings to him when you enter and when you exit, and from afar.'
ai.seo_question: What is the proper way to greet the Prophet Muhammad when visiting his grave in the mosque?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Rida (AS) establishes the normative etiquette for Ziyarah by affirming that greeting the Prophet (PBUH) is obligatory upon both entry and exit, countering those who merely pass by without salutation. The Imam’s personal practice of not approaching the grave directly, yet still offering salam from a distance, highlights the balance between reverence and the specific architectural context of the Prophet's mosque in Medina. This hadith serves as a primary textual basis for the Shia practice of offering salam at the threshold or within the prayer hall rather than exclusively at the immediate foot of the grave.
